transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~41 mins
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ramos (Redwood CSM), Evan Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Park (Orchard), Amit Rao (Orchard CTO), Sara Holt (Orchard Procurement), Benji Cole (Orchard Platform)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in with Orchard Medical to confirm their capacity uplift (EU burst), timeline for adding an EU region with private VPC option, and to align contract amendment steps. Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot bench plan, KMS requirements and procurement timeline.

Topics covered:
- Current consumption and projected ramp for Q2/Q3
- EU region onboarding (private VPC vs hosted EU)
- Contract amendment / PO timing for 6-month uplift (burst capacity)
- Security/compliance: KMS, data residency, audit logs
- Bench/validation plan and rollback/fallback policies

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sophie Chen: alright everyone thanks for hopping on, um we wanted to do a quick renewal and onboarding sync — keep it tight, 40 minutes — is that still good for folks?
[00:10] Dr. Lina Park: yes that works, quick heads up we have a 3pm internal so if needed we'll drop but should be fine.
[00:18] Amit Rao: same here, we want clarity on the EU burst because regulatory folks are breathing down our necks.
[00:23] Miguel Ramos: high level — Orchard's current prod commit ends in May, you flagged needing extra capacity in June for a pilot in the EU, correct Lina?
[00:31] Lina Park: yeah correct — basically more inference throughput for our clinical triage models, mostly p99 latency sensitive. We're trying to keep latency under 120ms for critical paths.
[00:40] Evan Patel: just to clarify, are we measuring 120ms for generation token latency or end-to-end request? because that affects batching and kernel selection.
[00:48] Lina Park: it's end-to-end, user-facing inference (single-turn), so prefer single-request low latency, but we can tolerate some batching on lower-priority routes.
[00:58] Sophie Chen: thanks — so two asks today: one, confirm what EU topology you want (hosted EU vs private VPC in eu-west1) and two, align commercial steps for a short-term 6 month burst, with option to extend.
[01:10] Amit Rao: procurement side we prefer a sealed PO for the uplift and an amendment to the master services agreement. Sara, any timeline?
[01:17] Sara Holt: if terms are clear we can do a PO within 3 weeks, legal needs the amendment redlined but procurement is okay to move fast.
[01:26] Miguel Ramos: perfect — we'll plan to get a draft amendment and pricing worksheet to you by next Monday.
[01:32] Benji Cole: technical question — for VPC, how intrusive is the private control plane? We need to know if anything needs a whitelist on our side.
[01:40] Evan Patel: good question. For Redwood Private we do a customer-managed VPC peering and control plane sits in your account with minimal inbound rules — primarily egress to Redwood monitoring endpoints. We'll send a VPC runbook. Some of the names in the runbook may show up a bit mangled in the transcript, but you'll get the doc.
[01:57] Lina Park: also KMS — we have an HSM-backed KMS, can Redwood integrate or do you require rekeying?
[02:04] Sophie Chen: we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations; for HSM-backed flows we have additional ops steps, Evan will note the gating items.
[02:12] Evan Patel: yes, we'll need the key policy and a short window for a test rotation. Also we'll want access to audit logs for that EU cluster.
[02:20] Amit Rao: audit logs are core, yes.
[02:22] Sophie Chen: on the performance side, Miguel — we recommended a small dedicated pool for the first 30 days to validate p99, then scale to burst. That keeps unit economics reasonable.
[02:32] Miguel Ramos: right, the recommendation we sent last week — dedicated slice plus burst capacity — will minimize cold-starts and levies. We'll include the exact vGPU counts in the worksheet.
[02:41] Benji Cole: can you explain the fallback policy? If EU capacity is saturated, do requests route to US and how does data residency work then?
[02:49] Evan Patel: by default we can route to a compatible model in another region but we flag it as a policy: for Orchard we can enforce no cross-border fallback for regulated routes. We can implement a strict region-only policy for the endpoints handling PHI. For non-regulated endpoints we can allow fallback.
[03:05] Lina Park: that's critical — for the clinical triage path we need region-only. For analytics and training-trigger routes we can allow fallback.
[03:12] Sophie Chen: noted. we'll make that a per-route policy.
[03:16] Miguel Ramos: timeline check — you said you want EU live June 15 for the pilot?
[03:22] Lina Park: June 15 is ideal, maybe stretch to June 22 if procurement lags.
[03:28] Sophie Chen: sounds doable. For that we need: PO by first week of March, run bench the week of March 8 so we can tune kernels and quantization, and deployment rehearsals mid-May.
[03:40] Sara Holt: procurement can hit PO by March 23 at the latest; earlier if the amendment is clean.
[03:46] Amit Rao: one more thing — what about model version pinning and rollbacks? We need a canary for any model swap.
[03:54] Evan Patel: Redwood supports stable version pinning per-route with canary rollouts. You can set percentage traffic for canary and automatic rollback on regression signals. We also capture token-level cost so you can see spend impact.
[04:06] Benji Cole: regarding bench tests — we'll provide a traffic trace (CSV) and a small sample dataset, should we obfuscate PHI?
[04:12] Lina Park: yes obfuscate PHI, but keep request distribution intact. Benji will do that.
[04:17] Evan Patel: perfect. we'll run the bench in our EU staging with same instance types you intend to use. Expect 48 hour run and a readout.
[04:25] Sophie Chen: commercial note — for a 6-month uplift we can offer a blended uplift rate and credit if you commit early to a 12-month extension. Miguel will put numbers in the worksheet.
[04:34] Sara Holt: we can consider a 12-month if the BL is favorable, but procurement needs clear exit language.
[04:39] Miguel Ramos: understoood. We'll add an opt-in 12 month clause with a 30 day cancellation window for the burst portion.
[04:46] Lina Park: what's the expected p99 delta when going from hosted to dedicated with quantization? We need to make sure clinical threshold holds.
[04:54] Evan Patel: typical p99 improvement is about 10-25ms depending on seq length and quantization strategy; with no-quant (FP16) you'll see the best latency, quantized gives cost reduction with a small latency tradeoff. We'll include model-specific numbers in the bench readout.
[05:10] Amit Rao: ok, let's make sure the bench includes both seq len profiles.
[05:15] Benji Cole: action on us is to share seq distribution and anonymized payloads by March 4.
[05:21] Sophie Chen: got it. any other security concerns?
[05:24] Sara Holt: SOC2 type II report and ISO attestation? We have to present them to our security steering committee.
[05:31] Miguel Ramos: we have up-to-date SOC2 and can share our ISO doc — I'll attach to the worksheet email.
[05:36] Lina Park: also need proof of encryption in transit and at rest with customer keys.
[05:40] Evan Patel: both supported; we'll include KMS integration steps and sample audit logs.
[05:44] Sophie Chen: wrapping — recap of decisions: Orchard wants EU region with private VPC for regulated routes, 6-month burst starting ~June 15 with potential 12-month option. Procurement to aim for PO in March. Redwood to run bench, share pricing worksheet and VPC/KMS runbooks.
[05:58] Amit Rao: that aligns, thanks.
[06:00] Sara Holt: one administrative ask — can you put the pricing in a line itemized spreadsheet? that's easiest for us.
[06:06] Miguel Ramos: yes, line-itemized worksheet will be in the Monday deliverable.
[06:11] Benji Cole: we'll get the traces to Evan by March 4.
[06:15] Lina Park: and we'll confirm go/no-go by March 9 after internal review.
[06:19] Sophie Chen: great. Any final q's?
[06:22] (brief silence)
[06:24] Amit Rao: none here. Thank you.
[06:26] Sophie Chen: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the worksheet and runbook. Miguel will own the commercial thread. Evan will own the bench. Benji and Sara will coordinate on the technical and procurement pieces.
[06:40] End of meeting.
